source.title: Selective Weak-to-Strong Generalization
source.authors: Hao Lang; Fei Huang; Yong-Bin Li

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports naive weak-label fine-tuning and performance gap recovered (PGR), the original intervention and measure, alongside its selective variant on NLP tasks.
record.gate_note: Tables 2 and 3 report PGR for naive fine-tuning, the proposed selective method, and alternative loss methods on three tasks with two weak supervisors. Table 4 reports PGR ablations. The paper also reports P(IK) AUROC and downstream accuracy for other analyses; those do not report PGR for the claim's weak-to-strong effect and are not rows here. Table 5 reports accuracy, not PGR.
record.test_reason: The study uses the Burns et al. setup and codebase: weak supervisor, naive weak-label fine-tuning, strong ceiling and PGR. It reports naive-fine-tuning PGR on three NLP tasks with two weak supervisors, which bears on V1 and V3. It also reports PGR for several training changes (auxiliary confidence, product, adaptive, reverse-KL and JS losses, plus its own selective P(IK) method) against naive fine-tuning, which bears on V2.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors argue weak supervision need not always be used: selective self-labelling via P(IK) plus graph-smoothed weak labels beats all compared baselines on SciQ, BoolQ and CosmosQA with both weak supervisors. They also find positive naive PGR on all tasks and say P(IK) generalizes across tasks and difficulty.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the original W2SG benchmark setup and PGR measure, and includes naive weak-label fine-tuning as a baseline. The proposed method adds P(IK)-based selective use of self-labels and graph smoothing.
record.method_sensitivity: PGR varies with task, weak-supervisor model, and training method; several loss variants have different results from naive fine-tuning, and the proposed selective method exceeds naive fine-tuning in all six main task-by-supervisor comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: A P(IK) classifier trained on ARC with Qwen-14B generalizes to other tasks, with AUROC 89.34 on SciQ but 47.73 on GSM8K (Table 6, Fig. 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Strong models' self-knowledge (P(IK)) transfers across tasks and difficulty, usable to select self-labels in W2SG.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the PGR values. The PGR experiments use a single strong-student size (Qwen/Qwen-14B) and three binary NLP classification tasks; the authors note that their strong/weak distinction is only model size and may not capture differences in reasoning or planning ability.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported PGR results were left out. P(IK) AUROC results in Table 6 and Figure 3, and accuracy-only results in Table 5, were excluded because they do not report PGR for the weak-to-strong effect.

untested.parts: Only binary NLP classification (SciQ, BoolQ, CosmosQA), one student (Qwen-14B), two supervisors. No uncertainty or seeds reported.
Ensembling weak supervisors and bootstrapping were not tested.
Student size, chess, reward modelling, and representation-based predictors of PGR were not tested. Only two supervisor sizes.
Not tested: no exploitation, distribution-shift or error-similarity PGR results.
Not tested: no vision or other non-language experiments.

missing.what: Selective method with P(IK) trained on CosmosQA, Winogrande or ARC beats naive fine-tuning in accuracy on SciQ (88.10→89.80–90.70) and BoolQ (80.85→82.99–83.39). PGR is computable from the Table 3 weak and ceiling values. Bears on V2 robustness to the choice of P(IK) training data.

record.verdict_notes: The method-comparison and ablation rows should link to V2 only. V3 applies to the naive rows (task and supervisor-size variation). The ablation rows used the full method as baseline; they were re-based to naive fine-tuning for V2. The authors say their method 'significantly outperforms', but no uncertainty or seeds are reported, so small differences (under 1 PGR point) should be read as no change. The study is not an original source, and it was published at AAAI 2026.

versions.untested_parts: Tests the basic effect only on the listed binary NLP classification tasks, with Qwen/Qwen-14B as student and GPT-2 or Qwen/Qwen-1.8B as weak supervisor.
Tests selective W2SG and several loss variants; does not test ensembling weak supervisors.
PGR comparisons cover three NLP tasks, two weak-model sizes and one strong-model size. It does not test PGR across student sizes, chess, reward modelling, or representations as predictors.
No own PGR test of supervisor-check failures, distribution-shift effects on W2SG performance, or error similarity.
No theoretical result about conditions forcing a student to beat its supervisor.
No vision or other non-language W2SG experiment.

relationships.reason: PGR rises over naive fine-tuning in every pair, e.g. 44.79→70.83 and 21.15→44.57. Ablated variants also beat naive (T2/T3-*-ours, T4-SciQ/BoolQ-noIK, T4-*-noGS, T4-*-MTL). No variance is reported.
